title: System boundaries, outcomes, and emergence
summary: Decide what the engineered system is accountable for, and what remains outside its authority.

title: Requirements, traceability, and assurance arguments
summary: Turn stakeholder needs into bounded, falsifiable obligations and credible evidence chains.

title: Architecture, interfaces, and design tradeoffs
summary: Separate functional responsibilities from physical choices, and reason about the interfaces that join them.

title: Model semantics, viewpoints, and digital traceability
summary: Know which claims a model can support and how its meaning survives revisions.

title: State machines, contracts, and distributed failures
summary: Explain why correct local code may yield incorrect system behavior when messages and time intervene.

title: Uncertainty, statistical evidence, and Bayesian decisions
summary: Distinguish uncertainty about outcomes from uncertainty about models and assumptions.

title: Queueing, congestion, and discrete-event simulation
summary: Understand why variability and utilization make response times nonlinear.

title: Stocks, feedback, controls, and numerical stability
summary: Connect feedback-loop stories to reproducible models with units and stability conditions.

title: Reliability, hazard controls, and resilience
summary: Reason from failure pathways to layered controls, while acknowledging common causes.

title: Multiobjective decisions, Pareto tradeoffs, and information value
summary: Defend architecture choices without hiding feasibility constraints or stakeholder preferences.

title: Digital threads, model credibility, and configuration provenance
summary: Make the connection between models, tests, and decisions trustworthy across tools and revisions.

title: Systems of systems, enterprise governance, and complex adaptation
summary: Understand why mission outcomes depend on independently governed constituents and human incentives.

title: Safety engineering: from hazards to enforceable constraints
summary: Build a safety argument from unsafe control actions, causal scenarios, controls, and residual uncertainty.

title: Human factors: design for decisions made under pressure

title: Cybersecurity engineering: threats, trust boundaries, and recovery
summary: Connect assets, adversary actions, architecture controls, detection, and test evidence.

title: Experimental design: ask a question the evidence can answer
summary: Build factorial experiments, control confounding, estimate interactions, and plan meaningful decisions.

title: Reliability, availability, and maintenance are different claims
summary: Connect failure processes, repair queues, spare parts, common causes, and mission continuity.

title: Robust optimization: feasibility before preference
summary: Compare alternatives across constraints, uncertainty sets, Pareto fronts, and regret.

title: Simulation credibility: verification, validation, and decision relevance
summary: Distinguish correct code from a credible model and trace uncertainty from inputs to decisions.

title: Engineering economics: lifecycle costs, options, and organizational value
summary: Turn architecture choices into transparent cost, discounting, and option-value arguments.
